audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with Psalm 95 citation; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Jesus/Moses, house imagery, Psalm 95 warning, unbelief, mutual exhortation.

verses.restored: Therefore, holy siblings, partners of heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,

familiar.text: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;

modern.text: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

original.text: Ὅθεν, ἀδελφοὶ ἅγιοι, κλήσεως ἐπουρανίου μέτοχοι, κατανοήσατε τὸν ἀπόστολον καὶ ἀρχιερέα τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν ⸀Ἰησοῦν,

verses.restored: trustworthy to the One who made/appointed him, as also Moses was in all his house.

familiar.text: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.

modern.text: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.

original.text: πιστὸν ὄντα τῷ ποιήσαντι αὐτὸν ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ⸀ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: For this one has been considered worthy of more glory than Moses, as the builder of a house has more honor than the house.

familiar.text: For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.

modern.text: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.

original.text: πλείονος γὰρ ⸂οὗτος δόξης⸃ παρὰ Μωϋσῆν ἠξίωται καθʼ ὅσον πλείονα τιμὴν ἔχει τοῦ οἴκου ὁ κατασκευάσας αὐτόν·

verses.restored: For every house is built by someone, but the One building all things is Divine.

familiar.text: For every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.

modern.text: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

original.text: πᾶς γὰρ οἶκος κατασκευάζεται ὑπό τινος, ὁ ⸀δὲ πάντα κατασκευάσας θεός.

verses.restored: And Moses was trustworthy in all his house as servant, into witness of things to be spoken,

familiar.text: And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;

modern.text: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.

original.text: καὶ Μωϋσῆς μὲν πιστὸς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ὡς θεράπων εἰς μαρτύριον τῶν λαληθησομένων,

verses.restored: but Messiah as Son over his house, whose house we are, if indeed we hold fast the boldness and boast of hope.

familiar.text: But Christ as a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.

modern.text: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast. Do Not Harden Your Hearts (Psalms 95:1–11)

original.text: Χριστὸς δὲ ὡς υἱὸς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ· ⸀ὃς οἶκός ἐσμεν ἡμεῖς, ⸀ἐὰν τὴν παρρησίαν καὶ τὸ καύχημα τῆς ⸀ἐλπίδος κατάσχωμεν.

verses.restored: Therefore, just as holy Spirit says: Today, if you hear his voice,

familiar.text: Wherefore (as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will hear his voice,

modern.text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,

original.text: Διό, καθὼς λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε,

verses.restored: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, according to day of testing in the wilderness,

familiar.text: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:

modern.text: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,

original.text: μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς ἐν τῷ παραπικρασμῷ, κατὰ τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ πειρασμοῦ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ,

verses.restored: where your ancestors tested by trial and saw my works forty years.

familiar.text: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.

modern.text: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

original.text: οὗ ⸀ἐπείρασαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ⸂ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ⸃ καὶ εἶδον τὰ ἔργα μου

verses.restored: Therefore I was displeased with that generation and said: They always wander in the heart, and they did not know my ways.

familiar.text: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.

modern.text: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’

original.text: τεσσεράκοντα ἔτη· διὸ προσώχθισα τῇ γενεᾷ ⸀ταύτῃ καὶ εἶπον· Ἀεὶ πλανῶνται τῇ καρδίᾳ· αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὰς ὁδούς μου·

verses.restored: As I swore in my anger: They shall not enter into my rest.

familiar.text: So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.)

modern.text: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” The Peril of Unbelief

original.text: ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου· Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου.

verses.restored: Watch, siblings, lest there be in any of you a harmful heart of untrust, in standing away from living Divine.

familiar.text: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.

modern.text: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

original.text: βλέπετε, ἀδελφοί, μήποτε ἔσται ἔν τινι ὑμῶν καρδία πονηρὰ ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος,

verses.restored: But encourage one another each day, as long as it is called Today, so that none of you may be hardened by deceit of sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.

modern.text: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.

original.text: ἀλλὰ παρακαλεῖτε ἑαυτοὺς καθʼ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, ἄχρις οὗ τὸ Σήμερον καλεῖται, ἵνα μὴ σκληρυνθῇ ⸂τις ἐξ ὑμῶν⸃ ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας·

verses.restored: For we have become partners of Messiah, if indeed we hold the beginning of our confidence firm until completion,

familiar.text: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;

modern.text: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.

original.text: μέτοχοι γὰρ ⸂τοῦ Χριστοῦ γεγόναμεν⸃, ἐάνπερ τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς ὑποστάσεως μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν κατάσχωμεν.

verses.restored: while it is said: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.

familiar.text: While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.

modern.text: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

original.text: ἐν τῷ λέγεσθαι· Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, Μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς ἐν τῷ παραπικρασμῷ.

verses.restored: For who, having heard, rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?

familiar.text: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.

modern.text: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?

original.text: τίνες γὰρ ἀκούσαντες παρεπίκραναν; ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντες οἱ ἐξελθόντες ἐξ Αἰγύπτου διὰ Μωϋσέως;

verses.restored: And with whom was he displeased forty years? Was it not with those who sinned/misaligned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

familiar.text: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?

modern.text: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

original.text: τίσιν δὲ προσώχθισεν τεσσεράκοντα ἔτη; οὐχὶ τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασιν, ὧν τὰ κῶλα ἔπεσεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ;

verses.restored: And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not to those who disobeyed?

familiar.text: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?

modern.text: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?

original.text: τίσιν δὲ ὤμοσεν μὴ εἰσελεύσεσθαι εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν;

verses.restored: And we see that they were not able to enter because of untrust.

familiar.text: So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.

modern.text: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.

original.text: καὶ βλέπομεν ὅτι οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν εἰσελθεῖν διʼ ἀπιστίαν.

translation_notes: Moses is honored as trustworthy servant; Hebrews' comparison must not become anti-Moses or anti-Jewish.
Psalm 95's Today is a living summons; mutual encouragement prevents hardening.
Unbelief/untrust is relational refusal, not intellectual doubt punished as such.
safety_note: Warning passages should be handled pastorally: they call for communal encouragement and responsiveness, not terror-based control.
